ID: PM-40973
Link (for internal use): https://bitwarden.atlassian.net/browse/PM-40973

> **Note:** the following analysis was produced by Claude Code (Opus 5) on my behalf.

Root cause looks like a **race condition on a non-thread-safe `StringBuilder`** in the Setup project, not a configuration problem.

In [`util/Setup/Helpers.cs`](https://github.com/bitwarden/server/blob/main/util/Setup/Helpers.cs), `Exec` shares one `StringBuilder` between both stream handlers:

```csharp
var result = new StringBuilder();                       // not thread-safe

process.OutputDataReceived += (_, e) => { ...; result.AppendLine(e.Data); };  // line 138
process.ErrorDataReceived  += (_, e) => { ...; result.AppendLine(e.Data); };
```

.NET pumps stdout and stderr on separate threadpool threads, so when both are captured the two `AppendLine` calls race and corrupt the builder's internal chunk bookkeeping — which surfaces exactly as `ArgumentException: Destination is too short` from `StringBuilder.AppendWithExpansion`. It's thrown on the reader thread, hence unhandled.

Why it appears in 2026.7.0: #7942 added the legacy `identity.pfx` re-encryption step at the top of `Update()` and switched that call to `returnStderr: true`, making it the only call site capturing **both** streams. The thread-unsafe `Exec` itself came from the earlier refactor in #7494. Whether it crashes depends on thread interleaving, so it's intermittent.

Impact: `run.sh` uses `set -e` and runs `updatebw` → `updateDatabase`. In my log the crash was in the second Setup run, so containers restarted on 2026.7.0 but the **database migration never ran**. `./bitwarden.sh updatedb` re-runs just that step (retry until it gets through).

Possible fix: give stdout and stderr separate builders (or lock the appends).

Hi there,

I am unable to reproduce this issue, it has been escalated for further investigation. If you have more information that can help us, please add it below. 

Thanks!
Claude analysis matches what we see - threading issue on non-thread-safe StringBuilder (appending both stdout and stderr to the same builder). So it is matter of timing - harder to reproduce.
I'm seeing this exact same issue myself, intermittent. Started the day my self-hosted Docker instance upgraded to 2026.7.0.

Seen once (of many failures — the rest are all the line-138 AppendLine variant), same 2026.7.0, a second manifestation from the same Helpers.Exec:

```
System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: ... (Parameter 'chunkLength')
   at System.Text.StringBuilder.ToString()
   at Bit.Setup.Helpers.Exec(...) in /source/util/Setup/Helpers.cs:line 148
   at Bit.Setup.Program.Update(Application application) in /source/util/Setup/Program.cs:line 167
```

This one crashed 7 seconds in, before any container work, so it's the first Exec call in Update rather than the migration phase. Worth noting the ToString() read is on the other side of the same StringBuilder from line 138's AppendLine — a fix guarding only the callback appends may not cover this path.
I have the same Issue on RHEL 9.8

summary: WebAuthn devices beyond previous max do not work as 2FA
description:
### Steps To Reproduce

1. Register 6 or more WebAuthn devices at [vault.bitwarden.com](https://vault.bitwarden.com/#/settings/security/two-factor)
2. Log out
3. Attempt to login
4. When prompted, attempt to use 6th or later device registered as 2FA security key


### Expected Result

Website accepts the key and user successfully logs in.

### Actual Result

Get an error "Try a different security key. You're using a security key that's not registered with this website".

### Screenshots or Videos

_No response_

### Additional Context

All previously registered security keys (up to the previous limit of 5) work as expected still.
Behavior is identical across Brave and firefox on macOS, Debian 13 and Windows 11. 
Keys register and save successfully but all keys past the former 5 key limit do not work as a second factor 
Not sure about passkey login, my hunch is the behavior is the same. 
Happy to test that hypothesis and work this issue if needed. Would love a chance to work on some FIDO2/WebAuthn stuff/contribute to one of my favorite OSS projects.
